questions.q: **Shift+F3** in MS Word —
options: Changes the case of selected text (lower/UPPER/Capitalise)
questions.solution: **Shift+F3** cycles the case of the selection in Word — press repeatedly to march lower → UPPER → Capitalise Each Word. (In Excel, plain Shift+F3 opens Insert Function instead.)

questions.q: Which shows memories in **decreasing order of speed**?
questions.solution: Speed falls as you move away from the CPU: **Registers → Cache → RAM → Hard disk** (size and cheapness rise in the same direction).

questions.q: One **byte** consists of how many bits?
questions.solution: **1 byte = 8 bits** — the definition every other conversion builds on.

questions.q: Which technology was used in the **first** generation of computers?
questions.solution: First-generation machines (ENIAC, UNIVAC-I, EDVAC) were built around **vacuum tubes**, which made them room-sized, hot and unreliable.

questions.q:
Choose the correct order of the parts to make a meaningful sentence.

**1.** A museum is a storehouse of history. **P:** Each artefact tells a story of its time. **Q:** Visitors can see weapons, coins and paintings there. **R:** Curators work hard to preserve these treasures. **S:** Some pieces are thousands of years old. **6.** A trip to a museum is a walk through time.
questions.solution: **Q** (specific exhibits, 'there' = museum) → **P** (each artefact = those exhibits) → **S** (their age) → **R** ('these treasures' = the pieces) → S6. QPSR.
questions.shortcut: General→specific: claim, examples, then 'these treasures' needs the pieces before it.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Green with envy
options: new to a job and inexperienced
questions.solution: Green = envy, so *green with envy* = **very jealous**. 'Inexperienced' is a different use of green (a greenhorn), not this idiom.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

One who comes into a foreign country to live there permanently
questions.solution: im/in = in → one who comes IN = **immigrant**. An emigrant leaves his own country (e-/ex- = out); the same person is an emigrant there and an immigrant here.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  I will call you when I ___ home.
questions.solution: The time clause after 'when' takes the simple present for future meaning → **reach**.

questions.q: The jewelled **Peacock Throne (Takht-i-Taus)** was made for —
questions.solution: The **Peacock Throne** was made under **Shah Jahan** (by goldsmith Bebadal Khan) — taken away by Nadir Shah in 1739.
questions.shortcut: Peacock Throne = Shah Jahan → Nadir Shah.

questions.q: Tuberculosis is caused by a:
questions.solution: TB is caused by the bacterium ***Mycobacterium tuberculosis***, discovered by Robert Koch (1882). The **BCG** vaccine protects against it and the **Mantoux** test detects infection.

questions.q: The autobiography **A Shot at History** is associated with which sportsperson?
questions.solution: **A Shot at History: My Obsessive Journey to Olympic Gold** - shooter **Abhinav Bindra**, co-written with Rohit Brijnath.

questions.q: Which of the following constitutes M1 (narrow money) in India?
options: Currency with the public + time deposits with banks
Currency with the public + demand deposits with banks + other deposits with the RBI
Currency with the public + post office savings deposits
questions.solution: **M1 = currency with the public + demand (current/savings) deposits with banks + 'other deposits' with the RBI.** Time deposits enter only M2/M3; post-office deposits sit outside M1, and M3 = M1 + time deposits (broad money).
questions.shortcut: Narrow = instantly spendable — currency plus demand deposits only.

questions.q: The longest diagonal of a regular hexagon is $12$ cm. The area of the hexagon is:
questions.solution:
Longest diagonal $= 2a \Rightarrow a = \frac{12}{2} = 6$ cm.

$K = \frac{3\sqrt3}{2} \times 36 = 54\sqrt3$ sq cm.
questions.shortcut: Side = half the long diagonal: $6$; area $\frac{3\sqrt3}{2} \times 36 = 54\sqrt3$. Trap: $108\sqrt3$ (took the diagonal as the side).

questions.q: Find the value of $\sqrt[3]{0.000064}$.
questions.shortcut: 6 decimal places → 2 decimal places in the root.

questions.q: Find the value of $\sqrt[3]{9261}$.
questions.solution:
Groups of three from the right: 9 | 261 → a two-digit root.
Cube ends in 1 → root ends in 1 (or 9 wait: only 1³ ends in 1). First group $8 \le 9$ → tens digit 2. Root = **21**.
questions.shortcut: Unit-digit map: cube ends 1 → root ends 1; 2³ = 8 fits under 9.

questions.q: Two chords $AB$ and $CD$ intersect inside a circle at $X$. If $AX = 6$ cm, $XB = 8$ cm and $CX = 4$ cm, the length of $XD$ is:
questions.solution: Intersecting chords: $AX \cdot XB = CX \cdot XD \Rightarrow 48 = 4 \times XD \Rightarrow XD = 12$ cm.
questions.shortcut: $\frac{6 \times 8}{4} = 12$ cm. Trap: $16$ cm ($4 + 12$, the whole chord).

questions.q: In a town, **65% of adults read a Hindi paper, 40% read an English paper and 20% read both**. If **3,000 adults read neither**, how many adults are there in the town?
questions.shortcut: Find the percent of the known group, then scale up.

questions.q: Which set of signs will make **18 ? 6 ? 3 ? 4 = 24** correct?
questions.solution:
Put each option's signs into the blanks from left to right, then use BODMAS:

- −, +, ×: 18 − 6 + 3 × 4 = 24 ✓
- +, ÷, ×: 18 + 6 ÷ 3 × 4 = 26 ✗
- ÷, ×, +: 18 ÷ 6 × 3 + 4 = 13 ✗
- ×, ÷, −: 18 × 6 ÷ 3 − 4 = 32 ✗

Only **−, +, ×** balances.
questions.shortcut: Check the target size first: a big right side needs ×; a small one needs ÷ or −.

questions.q: **Rita's son is Amit. Amit's son is Karan.** How is **Karan related to Rita**?
questions.solution: Rita → Amit → Karan: two generations down from Rita, male → **grandson**.
questions.shortcut: Two down-arrows from Rita = grandchild; Karan is a boy → grandson.

questions.q: If **sky is called sea**, **sea is called water**, **water is called air**, and **air is called cloud**, where do **fishes** live?
questions.solution: Fishes live in the **sea** (reality). But 'sea' is called **water** in this code → fishes live in **water**.
questions.shortcut: Find the real answer first, then apply the rename — one substitution step.
